chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them:

A person who apostasizes from Islam is to be separated from his wife, his slaughtered animal is not to be eaten, and he is to be given an opportunity to repent for three days. If he returns, otherwise he is killed on the fourth day, provided he is of sound mind.

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion from which the person has apostatized
key_terms.الْمُرْتَدَّ: the one who has apostasized from Islam
key_terms.امْرَأَتُهُ: his wife, from whom he is to be separated
key_terms.ذَبِيحَتُهُ: his slaughtered animal, which is not lawful to eat
key_terms.صَحِيحَ الْعَقْلِ: being of sound mind and legally accountable
key_terms.يُسْتَتَابُ: he is asked to repent and given a chance to return

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the legal ruling for apostasy in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning the apostate from Islam, including separation from his wife, the impermissibility of eating his slaughtered animal, and a three-day period for tawbah (repentance). If he returns, he is spared; if not, he is subject to execution on the fourth day, on the condition that he is of sound mind.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3547 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers, peace be upon them:

"A person who apostasizes from Islam is to be separated from his wife, his slaughtered meat is not to be eaten, and he is to be given an opportunity to repent for three days. If he repents, he is spared, but if he does not repent, he is killed on the fourth day, provided he is of sound mind."
